checks.claim: Same semantic role → same type role
checks.observed: Both sections use one section-title, subsection-title and reading-copy rule. Independent computed values match across A/B at both viewports; all six reminders share one style.

The 16/17/18px reminder differences collapse to one 16px bold role. Desktop title/section/subsection use 48/32/24px; mobile 40/24/20px. Bold headings, regular reading copy and existing structural whitespace provide additional contrast.
Rendered type sizes are a subset of 14/16/20/24/32/40/48px. The default vocabulary is used without a new arbitrary size set.
14px metadata/orientation is retained for its semantic purpose. It is not rounded to 12/16 merely to follow the unchanged spatial grid.

Three resolved families become Arial only. Computed requested weights are 400/700; CDP reports ArialMT and Arial-BoldMT, and font-synthesis is none. Long reading stays regular rather than bold everywhere. Before Guide Sans registered only regular ArialMT while requesting 800/900; those synthesized/unsupported treatments are removed.

The actual English long-reading measure becomes 569.5px desktop / 342px mobile at 16px with 25.6px line-height. Existing paragraph gap stays 16px. Desktop non-final lines are 66–87 characters (mostly 70–80); mobile non-final lines 36–50. These are observations, not absolute 60–80 gates. Actual viewport captures show readable paragraphs without horizontal clipping.

Before, the 108px count outweighed a 22px page title and 160px decorative circle competed with it. After, the title is 48/40px bold, secondary count 32px regular muted, circle 96px. In observed first screens, title/read task leads; the reference collection is subordinate beside/below it and the action remains visible.

Mobile changes only the page/section/subsection role scales while reading/body/metadata remain legible. The mobile title reads Make every / handover / easy to follow.; desktop Make every handover / easy to follow. There is no inherited 0.75 scaling. Semantic content, heading order and action remain.
